hints: A suffix automaton represents each distinct substring as a path.
Unlike the distinct version, count each path endpoint by the number of occurrences of that substring.
Propagate occurrence counts along suffix links, then use weighted path counts to select k.
analogy: A branch contains repeated copies of its word as well as all longer words beginning with it.
example: For aba, sorted substrings are a, a, ab, aba, b, ba; k=2 gives a.
algorithm: Build a suffix automaton, marking each non-clone state created for a new prefix with count 1 and clones with 0. Propagate counts to suffix links in decreasing length. Compute ways[v]=sum over transitions v->u of (occ[u]+ways[u]). Traverse transitions in character order, skipping groups by their sizes; after taking an edge, consume occ[u] copies of the current substring before continuing. Use wide counts.
correctness: Every substring path ends at a state whose occurrence count is its number of end positions. Weighted path counts therefore list each substring with exactly its multiplicity, and lexicographic branch selection returns the requested copy.
complexity: For n characters over 26 letters, O(26n) time and O(26n) space.
